what: Pressing the menu button opens the panel by growing a flower-shaped (or supplied SVG-shaped) hole from the exact center of the button, from 0 up to the scale that covers all four screen corners (distance to the farthest corner ÷ shape radius × 2), accelerating over .6s with cubic-bezier(.7,0,.84,0). Closing returns to the same spot over .6s with cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1), overshooting once before shrinking. Shape coordinates stay as they are and it is scaled only with transform (it also closes with Esc · a click on the panel background · fx:close)

options.ease-open: Open curve — a css name or four numbers (comma-separated), default 0.7,0,0.84,0
options.[data-fx-part=trigger·panel·shape]: Open button · cover panel · hole shape <path>(If none, six petals)
options.fx:close: Sending to the element closes it

use: …

from.where: shared.js Header — original Iris (#iris-clip-nav-path · open .6s cubic-bezier(.7,0,.84,0) · close .6s cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1)). With the same calculation, page transitions also close as a leaf shape onto the pressed spot and open as a flower shape from the center (swup hook)

note: The original uses the same iris shape for page transitions (swup) too. The transition lives in startSwup in the site’s shared.js
